messages:
maria: Heads-up — while validating mi250 int4 paths for the new quant profiles I hit a kernel-selection miss that routed the request to the generic fallback path (much slower). attaching quick profile link.

runtime-ci: profile uploaded: https://ci.redwood/snapshots/1734567890 (html + flamegraph)

ashwin: can you paste the relevant log snippet here?

maria: sure, pasted excerpt from the runtime logs:
```
2026-03-10T12:34:56Z kernel_lookup: model=redwood-3b quant=int4 seq_len=2048 arch=mi250 kernels_found=[]
2026-03-10T12:34:56Z routing: fallback -> cpu_generic_conv
2026-03-10T12:34:56Z perf: latency=382ms batch=1 kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.04
```

liam: is this strictly seq-dependent or combined with batch/kv state? looks like >1024 triggers different tiling policy on mi250 (we sometimes have missing tiled kernels for int4).

maria: observed only when seq_len > 1024 AND quant=int4. seq<=1024 picks amdgpu_fp16_tile kernel as expected.

olivia: were you running with continuous batching + KV caching enabled? kv evictions can change key shapes and that sometimes influences which kernel signatures get probed at runtime.

ashwin: our autotuner currently skipped int4 probes for mi250 in the last rollout (it was offline). so the autotune catalog likely doesn't contain signatures for int4 @ >1k seq. that's why kernel_lookup returns empty.

maria: proposal: implement a soft-route policy — if a kernel signature is missing but an amdgpu candidate exists within a small perf delta (measured on nearby shapes), prefer GPU route for latency-sensitive requests instead of immediately falling back to CPU. also seed autotuner with seq sizes [128,512,1024,2048] for int4 during package install / registration.

liam: caveat: older driver 5.x on some nodes crashes with certain tiled kernels at seq>2048. we need a driver-gating handshake: kernel.handshake_ok flag from registration and telemetry before we route production traffic.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: runtime/staging -> feature/soft-route-int4. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/soft-route-int4 (follow canary checks)

ashwin: I'll add an install-time autotune probe that runs small microbenchmarks across seq sizes and quant modes, writing results to /var/lib/runtime/autotune-cache.json; autotune cache will be consulted during kernel_lookup. fallback to remote-autotune if cache missing.

maria: :thumbsup: I'll attach perf numbers from the canary once it's up. immediate priority: hotfix routing to avoid CPU fallback for interactive latency-sensitive endpoints.

runtime-ci: canary test summary snapshot:
- seq=2048 quant=int4 batch=1: amdgpu tiled kernel latency 185ms vs fallback cpu_generic 380ms
- kv_cache hit reduced effective throughput by ~20% when route changed mid-token (prefix cache invalidation)
- autotune-cache populated with 128/512/1024/2048 entries on 3/4 staging nodes

olivia: create a console alert: "kernel_fallback_rate > 0.5% over 5m" and link to runbook. I'll add the dashboard panel and alert rule.

maria: thanks — I'll follow up with a short RFC for the autotune probe and the soft-route policy (will include telemetry fields we should emit).

ashwin: note for follow-up: add integration test that simulates sequence-length jitter + KV eviction to ensure we don't regress batching heuristics when kernels flip.

liam: sounds good. once canary is green we'll roll to dedicated nodes with driver gate.

maria: leaving logs & sample profiles in the thread link. ping me if you need quick reproducer.
